description: Please join us the last Monday of every month from 4-5pm PST, for the WISDOM Study monthly community forum! The WISDOM Study is a national, landmark research study working to revolutionize the way breast cancer is screened, detected, and risk-reduced. The WISDOM community is comprised of pioneering researchers and doctors, dedicated staff, patient advocates and ambassadors, study participants and community members who've come together to work toward our common goal. Our community forum is an opportunity for us convene and discuss the latest topics in the field with input from our WISDOM Study clinicians and scientists. Most importantly, it's an opportunity to hear your questions and address the topics that are most important to our communities. All are welcome to this forum, so please share this information. For questions or concerns, please contact us at wisdomcommunity@ucsf.edu.

description: This event is in-person only, but open to UCSF clinicians, researchers, and educators. This talk presents Mindfulness-Based Health Promotion (MBHP), a mindfulness-based intervention (MBI) developed in Brazil and culturally adapted to Brazilian public policies. Drawing on more than a decade of work at the Mente Aberta Center (Federal University of São Paulo), the talk traces the cultural aspects of these practices in Brazil, their adaptation to Brazilian public policies, especially to our national health system (SUS), and the evidence supporting MBHP's effectiveness as a public policy tool for supported self-care and health equity. The presentation also reflects on the speaker's own relationship to contemplative practice and its integration with preventive and lifestyle medicine. Marcelo Demarzo, MD, PhD, is a physician specializing in Family Medicine, Sports Medicine, Preventive Medicine, and Lifestyle Medicine, and an expert (teacher, trainer and researcher) in secular, evidence-based mindfulness and compassion training. He is Associate Professor (Livre-Docente) at the Federal University of São Paulo (UNIFESP), Senior Fellow in Primary Health Care at the University of Oxford, and Visiting Researcher at UTS Sydney, the University of Melbourne, Universidad de Zaragoza, and Macau University of Science and Technology. He is a CNPq Research Productivity Fellow and holds a PhD in Experimental Pathology. In 2011 he founded the Mente Aberta Center at UNIFESP and developed the Mindfulness-Based Health Promotion (MBHP) protocol, now widely implemented across the Brazilian public health system (SUS). He is the Executive Director of CABSIN (Brazilian Academic Consortium for Integrative Health), a collaborative network of over 300 affiliated researchers advancing evidence-based Traditional, Complementary, and Integrative Medicine and informing Brazilian public health policy. He also serves as a consultant to the World Health Organization and is a global reference in mindfulness, supported self-care, and health promotion research. The Osher Center for Integrative Health hosts monthly research seminars that are open to the research and clinical community at large. Seminars are held from September to June and are generally virtual. Presentations cover a wide range of topics relating to integrative health, many with a focus on integrative health equity. Research Seminars are organized by Ariana Thompson-Lastad, PhD and Joanne Qina’au, PhD, MA, E-YT750. Please contact Julia Wu (julia.wu@ucsf.edu) with any questions., powered by Localist, the Community Event Platform

description: “High Blood Pressure in Kids: When to Worry and What to Do Next” Presented by: Alexandra Bicki, MD Pediatric nephrologist UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital San Francisco Planners expect learners to: 1. description: What helps people feel that they truly belong—and what happens when they do? Join the UCSF Climate and Belonging's Fostering Awareness Speaker Series on October 28th from 12:10–1:00 p.m. for The Science of Belonging, featuring UCSF’s Mica Estrada, PhD. Part of the Fostering Awareness: Dimensions of Belonging series, this session will explore the research behind belonging and the ways our environments, relationships, and everyday interactions can influence whether people feel valued, connected, and able to thrive. Dr. Estrada is Associate Dean of Opportunity & Engagement and Professor in the UCSF School of Nursing. Her research examines social influence, identity, values, kindness, well-being, mentorship, and approaches that strengthen inclusion and persistence in STEMM communities.
